edges.description: Recapitulates the RES-dependent intron splicing defect, with embryonic neural degeneration and death by 4 to 5 days post-fertilization.
edges.limitations: The mutant is a functional null, whereas the human allele is hypomorphic because of the stable truncated isoform, so the model shows the direction of the splicing defect but not its human severity. It dies as an embryo, so lipodystrophy, achalasia, corneal and hearing phenotypes cannot be assessed.

nodes.description: The nonsense substitution causes alternative splicing of BUD13 transcripts, producing a stable truncated protein instead of no protein. Its expression level differs between affected individuals and tracks disease expression and life expectancy, which the authors interpret as the residual function that sets severity and survival. Patient cells are therefore BUD13-deficient rather than BUD13-null. The node carries no outgoing causal edge on purpose: the truncated protein limits the downstream defects rather than causing them, and the schema has no edge type for a severity modifier, so the defects hang from the variant node and this node records the modulation.

nodes.description: BUD13 is a subunit of the RES complex, which in vertebrates is required for efficient splicing of a subset of short, GC-rich introns. Patient dermal fibroblasts show elevated intron retention. Loss of bud13 or the other RES subunits in zebrafish causes a global intron-splicing defect, and BUD13 deficiency in macrophages increases retention of BUD13-dependent introns and reduces the corresponding mature transcripts.

nodes.description: The only reported allele, homozygous in all five affected individuals. ClinVar classifies it Pathogenic for achalasia-progeroid syndrome on a single submission (review status "criteria provided, single submitter").

Patient dermal fibroblasts have nuclei with multiple invaginations, more pronounced in the three severely affected individuals. Overexpression of either BUD13 isoform normalizes nuclear morphology. The route from BUD13 deficiency to nuclear shape is not established.
